snapshot.required_tech_usage:
SPLIT VERDICT: the YouCam client is genuine, non-trivial, first-party code — and it is 100% dormant at runtime in the state a judge would encounter.

THE CODE IS REAL (not a wrapper around a sample request). lib/youcam/ is 213 lines of client plus 9 feature modules implementing the actual 4-step Perfect Corp contract: Bearer auth → File API POST returning a presigned PUT target → raw-byte PUT with the provider's signed x-amz-* headers merged in (with Content-Length deliberately stripped so fetch computes it) → flat-body POST to the /task/ endpoint (derived from the /file/ path by string replacement) → poll data.task_status until success/error with a 1.5s interval and 120s deadline. It has transient-retry on 429/5xx with 400ms*attempt backoff, a typed YouCamError carrying status and body, provider response interfaces (FileApiResponse, PollResponse), and real semantic knowledge of the API — e.g. skin.ts documents that "SD and HD concern sets cannot be mixed in one request", passes miniserver_args:{enable_mask_overlay:true} to get a presentable AR overlay rather than a transparent mask, filters out the API's extra meta rows (all, skin_age, resize_image), and picks the LOWEST-health concern's mask so the overlay matches the concern the plan names. apparel.ts maps categories to AI-Cloth's garment_category enum (upper_body/lower_body/full_body/auto) and handles src_/ref_ role prefixes. This is not stubbed and it is not scaffolding.

CALL SITES ARE REAL BUT UNIVERSALLY SHORT-CIRCUITED. Every feature module opens with the same guard — `if (env.youcamFixtures) return fixtureX(...)` — placed BEFORE any endpoint resolution. With YOUCAM_FIXTURES=1 (the committed default in .env.example, the state /healthz reports, and the state the access notes say every visitor gets) no YouCam HTTP request is ever constructed. I confirmed this behaviourally across the full concierge loop, all four studio kinds, and /api/dev/verify: every image URL returned was a local /fixtures/*.jpg and every raw payload was `{"fixture":true}`. Not dormant behind an obscure flag — dormant behind the DEFAULT and INTENDED demo configuration.

ENDPOINT COVERAGE, precisely: 8 slugs declared in config.ts. 7 have exactly one call site each (grep-verified). `lookVto` has ZERO call sites — dead config that nonetheless inflates the youcam_apis_wired:8 figure /healthz publishes as a cross-check. Of the 7 live-wired ones, only 4 (skinAnalysis, colorTone, apparelVto, lighting) can render anything a judge sees, because the 3 studio slugs are gated by HAS_STUDIO_RENDERS=false and 2 of those 3 (makeup, hairstyle) have URL slugs the code's own comment marks UNVERIFIED after 401s on the demo key.

CREDENTIALS: YOUCAM_API_KEY is present in .env.local (67 chars) and YOUCAM_CLIENT_SECRET (216 chars), so a units-on run is theoretically one env flip away. But nothing on disk proves that key currently authenticates — no saved task_id, no captured raw response, no probe log — and healthz deliberately does not probe it (correctly, since every YouCam task call burns finite units). Per standing order #1 I did not spend units to find out.

BOTTOM LINE FOR THE TECHNOLOGICAL IMPLEMENTATION CRITERION: the code would satisfy "genuine effort and a working, non-trivial implementation" on a read-through. It would fail "provable from the running product" — which is what the config's own 9/10 anchor demands — because at judging time, on the configuration judges are told to expect, the required technology executes not once.

Aphrodite is a genuinely strong, unusually self-honest local prototype with an unbuilt showroom. All four of its own verify gates are green right now (tsc clean, lint clean, build clean, 57/57 tests pass in 648ms), and I drove the core experience end to end in 4.3s: the skin read names dark_circle_v2=59 as the priority area, that number flows into a horizon-aware countdown, the color read (warm/Warm Spring) drives the garment pick, the garment is composited onto the photo, a lighting pass finishes it, and everything lands in one 8-row priced basket across skincare, apparel and accessories. Against that, five things a judge would hit today. verdict.bottom_line:
OFFICIAL: 26/50. Submission Depth & Presentation: 3/10 (diagnostic, not folded in). Stage One: FAIL on gates 2, 3 and 4 — so as of today this entry is not eligible, and the 26 is academic until that changes. No previous review, so this is the baseline.

The panel is unusually unanimous, and unusually sympathetic. Five judges independently reached the same shape: this is a real, well-engineered, unusually self-honest build with no showroom. lib/youcam/ implements the genuine four-step Perfect Corp contract with signed presigned PUTs, Content-Length deliberately stripped, poll-to-task_status, 429/5xx retry, and semantic knowledge of the API most entrants never reach (SD/HD concern sets cannot be mixed; enable_mask_overlay for a presentable overlay; the lowest-health concern's mask chosen so the overlay matches the concern the plan names). The fused chain the tiebreaker rewards is architecturally real and I watched it run in 4.3s. The honesty machinery — /healthz's three-state model that refuses to probe because probes burn units, degradation to text instead of a fabricated render, demo-mode labelling in the first viewport, a README that volunteers its own past mis-gendering bug — is better than most winners ship.

And a judge gets none of it. No DNS, no deploy artifact, no published video, and origin/main is 8 commits behind without app/healthz, without HACKATHON.md, and without the cutPreference field — so the one judge who follows the README's own clone command lands on the un-mitigated mis-gendering behaviour and a 404 on the self-check chapter. That is the single weakest link: one failure to deliver, billed five times.

Three findings go beyond "unfinished" into things that must be fixed on principle, not for points. The refine flow makes a confirmed false tone claim, reproducible in two taps from a bundled preset, on the exact tap the video script films — integrity risk #3, materialized. An uploaded selfie in demo mode receives a stranger's scores and mask under the label "read from your own photo". And the provenance ledger tells the judge four Perfect Corp APIs ran in a run where none did. All three are small, local fixes by a builder whose instincts are already right — the demo flag reaches four surfaces and misses two; the tone check exists in the honest branch and is missing from the other. This is a seam problem, not a culture problem.

Order of operations is not negotiable: merge to main (five minutes, closes an integrity violation and the clone trap), fix the tone claim and the ledger, deploy, publish the video, submit Devpost, then spend units exactly once and commit the receipt. After that, favour the tiebreaker — the fusion-chain diagram and one units-on run on camera are what convert a chain the panel could only read into one it can watch. Also fix the date parser: a product whose entire premise is the plan for a specific day currently cannot read a specific day, and the Impact judge was right to lead with it.

Cut before you add. The three studio APIs, the makeup basket row, the zero-delta check-in, the dead lookVto, the stale screenshots and the older reel are all costing credibility they cannot repay.
